commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Lynde, Cheerful Tormentor ({1}{U}{B}{R} legendary Human Warlock 2/4 deathtouch). Commander-legal per live Scryfall, not a Game Changer, released, no project exception. Oracle: whenever a Curse is put into your graveyard from the battlefield, return it attached to you at the beginning of the next end step; at the beginning of your upkeep you may attach a Curse attached to you to an opponent, and if you do, draw two. Plan (owner 2026-10-14): Curse recycling and control. Put Curses on opponents, deliberately send your own Curses to your graveyard (Despotic Scepter, Claws of Gix, Perilous Research, Braids, Demon of Fate's Design), Lynde returns them to you and moves one each upkeep for two cards; extra upkeeps (Paradox Haze, The Ninth Doctor, Obeka) and Curse copying (Copy Enchantment, Mirrormade, Estrid's Invocation, Clever Impersonator) scale it. Both adds are upkeep copy engines that make new Curses attached to you for Lynde to move, and both cuts are the Curses whose Lynde return damages your own board.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 (Optimized; owner-approved, registry ceiling 4), unchanged. Game Changers: 8 in both baseline and candidate; none of the adds is a Game Changer. Commander Spellbook: 0 included combos in baseline and candidate (almost-included 17 -> 22); no combo is added or lost.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Commander-first to Lynde's Oracle: each add makes Curses for Lynde to move. No generic Thassa's Oracle/Consultation or Breach package, no non-Curse Aura (Archnemesis class; Grievous Wound rejected for that reason), no mill Curse (Fraying Sanity class), and no owner-removed card (Curse of Oblivion, Curse of Chaos, Curse of Shallow Graves, Fraying Sanity, Crystal Chimes, Protean Thaumaturge, Sphinx of the Second Sun or the seven replaced lands) or owner-rejected card (Strionic Resonator, Beseech the Mirror, Shadow of the Second Sun, Valeria Richards, The Unluckiest Planeswalker, Jabs) is added. Distinctness (nonbasic names shared with the other 61 registry Archidekt exports; the aggregate ALL-DECKS export excluded; 90 nonbasic names): Garza Zol, Plague Queen 42; Solkanar the Swamp King 41; Nicol Bolas 40; Solkanar the Tainted 39; Mai and Zuko 39 (the same for baseline and candidate). The overlap is the Grixis mana base and staples (fetches, duals, Signets/Talismans, tutors, free counters). Lynde-specific against those five: the Curse suite (Thirst, Bloodletting, Misfortunes, Surveillance, Unbinding, Obsession, Fool's Wisdom and the rest), the own-Curse outlets (Despotic Scepter, Claws of Gix, Perilous Research, Braids, Demon of Fate's Design) and the extra-upkeep package (Paradox Haze, The Ninth Doctor, Obeka). Across the other registry exports Court of Vantress and Extravagant Replication each appear in 1 deck; Cruel Reality and Curse of Death's Hold appear in none.

whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Stack: Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Swan Song, Deflecting Swat. Board: Cyclonic Rift, Chaos Warp, Deadly Rollick, Damnation, Toxic Deluge, Blasphemous Act. Lynde's recursion makes Curse removal by opponents a card advantage for you. Removal grid B4 (12 events each): Cruel Reality and Death's Hold return to you in 6 and then harm you (6 and 4); Court and Replication are not Curses, so removal simply removes them (0 returns, 0 self-harm). The candidate loses two table locks (sacrifice-per-upkeep and anti-token) and gains two engines that can be destroyed without a Lynde return.

material_candidates.commander_synergy: A Curse token copy is not cast, so you choose the player it enchants (CR 303.4f): attach it to yourself and Lynde moves it to an opponent for two cards, or attach it straight to an opponent. Cruel Reality is a real symmetrical lock on an opponent and much more popular (5703/7774 versus 1705/7774). The not-monarch Court-copies-a-Curse loop is moderate confidence and not relied on. Token Curses cease to exist in the graveyard (CR 704.5d), so Lynde cannot recur them.
material_candidates.reason: Genuine swap 1: a repeatable, Lynde-feeding Curse copy engine replaces the one Curse whose Lynde return attacks your own board. Not an owner card.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Two swaps: two upkeep copy engines that make Curse tokens for Lynde to move (and copy Paradox Haze, Misfortunes or creatures) replace the two Curses whose Lynde return harms your own board. Cost: two table locks (Cruel Reality's sacrifice tax and Death's Hold's anti-token shrink), Court depends on keeping the monarchy, Replication costs six with no immediate effect, and both cuts are more popular on EDHREC. Game Changers stay at 8; lands 35; Spellbook 0 included; Bracket 4. Neither cut is an owner keep or add.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Pass C's lower-priority Curse of Chaos/Curse of Echoes test and the author's Strionic Resonator/Nightscape and Beseech the Mirror hypotheses were each staged as complete compare-only 100s and rejected (owner-removed or owner-rejected cards). Neither selected cut is an owner keep, so no owner-keep override alternative is needed; alternatives A and B split the two swaps.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Lynde returns every Curse attached to YOU, and two of the deck's Curses punish the player they are attached to on the way back: Cruel Reality's upkeep sacrifice still resolves against you after Lynde moves it (Lynde is the sacrifice in 42/96 B1 cells), and Curse of Death's Hold kills your X/1s before your upkeep (32/96). The engine works best with Curses that are harmless to hold for one turn.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Two genuine swaps: +Court of Vantress -Cruel Reality and +Extravagant Replication -Curse of Death's Hold (both MODERATE; both cuts are more popular on EDHREC). Pass C's requested tests were run; Curse of Chaos, Strionic Resonator and Beseech the Mirror stay rejected; Staff of Compleation is a staged trade. Every other challenger is dominated, owner-rejected, off-engine or invalid. RESEARCH_ONLY.
